Rachel Beyerlein — Career Lead at Le Wagon. Session: Panel Discussion — Women, Work & What’s Next: Navigating the Future of Work. May 30, 2026, 3:30 PM. In-person at District3. Rachel is a designer at heart — and that instinct has shaped everything she's touched across 13+ years in product, and visual design.
Her canvas has expanded over time. Today, as Career, Event, and Community Lead at Le Wagon Canada, she designs something harder to prototype: learning experiences and the communities around them, helping people navigate their own paths into tech. She also contributes to Tech Fleet, staying close to the work of learning and product development.
Her work has taken her from designing things, to designing experiences, to now helping others design their journeys.

Prisca Onyebuchi — AI Strategy Advisor. Session: AI-Ready for Your Career — Turning Fear into Opportunity. June 01, 2026, 12:00 PM. Online (virtual). Prisca Onyebuchi is the founder of PriscaSolutionsAI where she runs two sides of one practice. She teaches AI workshops for professionals who aren't developers, sessions where people bring real problems and leave knowing how to solve them with Claude Code, Claude Cowork, Claude in Chrome, and Claude in Excel, building agents, workflows, and automations they actually understand, not just use. For businesses scaling fast, she builds custom AI systems on the side: content engines, research automation, multi-market workflows, built clean, documented thoroughly, owned completely by the team that hired her. She is passionate about
public speaking and storytelling, and occasionally shares both on LinkedIn.

Lin Sok — Tech Founder and Community Builder. Session: Panel Discussion — Women, Work & What’s Next: Navigating the Future of Work. May 30, 2026, 3:30 PM. In-person at District3. Lin Sok is a Montreal, Canada based entrepreneur, financial advisor, tech founder, speaker, and community builder.
Lin was born during the Khmer Rouge regime, in a UNICEF refugee camp on the Thai/Cambodia border. As a baby, she and her family fled to Canada and landed in Ottawa, followed by Montreal. Always a top student during her childhood, Lin had her first child at the age of 19 and got married shortly after. They had three other children together, only to divorce when their youngest was only two.
Though life had its hiccups, excuses were never allowed, something Lin credits to her strict Buddhist upbringing.
Her mission is to help others break the cycle of excuses and believe they can create abundance in wealth, business, and life.
Today Lin is remarried to her wonderful spouse Billy, is a proud mother of four, a rescue dog mom to a black Labrador mix, and is dedicated to being the voice for those who feel unheard.

Dominique Pirolo — IBM & Ex-SAP Talent Leader. Session: Panel Discussion — Women, Work & What’s Next: Navigating the Future of Work. May 30, 2026, 3:30 PM. In-person at District3. Dominique Pirolo is a professional in Talent Resource in hiring for large corporations having worked with SAP, Morgan Stanley and now with IBM.
She is passionate about women in tech in advancing and advocating for their career advancement and empowerment.
She is also a Certified as a Professional Coach, graduated from Concordia University (PCC). Member of the International Coaching Federation for 15 years, providing coaching in the space of transition and career.

Samantha Bateman — Executive Recruiter and Founder of Integria Consulting. Session: Panel Discussion — Women, Work & What’s Next: Navigating the Future of Work. May 30, 2026, 3:30 PM. In-person at District3. Samantha Bateman is President of Integria Consulting, an executive search firm she has led for over 20 years, partnering with companies on critical leadership hires and high-stakes roles.
She is also the Co-Founder of Alynd, an AI platform designed to help organizations get aligned and organized before they start recruiting—bringing structure to a process that is often unclear and inconsistent.
A mother of two, Samantha has built and continues to grow her businesses while being intentional about protecting her time and showing up for her family—an experience that has shaped her perspective on leadership and the realities of building in today’s work environment.
With two decades of experience working closely with leadership teams, she brings a practical, no-nonsense view on how hiring decisions are made, where processes break down, and how companies can do better.

Natalie Loop — Founder, Alygra. Session: From Employee to Architect — Portfolio Career in the Age of AI. June 05, 2026, 4:00 PM. Online (virtual). Natalie Loop is the Founder & CEO of Alygra — a boutique fractional advisory firm helping tech startups build the HR, legal, and AI infrastructure they need to scale with intention.


With over 15 years of hands-on experience across startups, scale-ups, and global firms, Natalie has led People & Culture functions at every stage of growth — from first hire to Series B. She operates as a Fractional Chief People Officer for early-stage tech companies in Canada and Europe, embedding directly into founding teams to build cultures where people don't just perform — they stay, grow, and care.


Her work sits at the interSegment of people strategy, organizational design, and the future of work: how do companies stay human as they scale? How do leaders build trust in distributed, AI-augmented teams? What does sustainable growth actually look like for the people living it?


Beyond her client work, Natalie mentors founders as an HR & Entrepreneurship Advisor with Quebec tech, La Base entrepreneuriale HEC, Next AI, and Fintech Cadence — working alongside builders who see culture not as a perk, but as a competitive advantage

Jeffrey To — Psychology PhD candidate and public speaking coach for tech professionals. Session: Speed Networking Activity. May 30, 2026, 2:45 PM. In-person at District3. Jeffrey didn't start out confident. When he moved to Toronto at 16, he was so socially anxious he didn't make a friend his entire university orientation week. His first Toastmasters speech was memorized word-for-word, rehearsed until it was airtight — the only way he knew how to get through it.


Today, he teaches classes of 800+ students with no notes, no script, and no safety net. He's a PhD researcher in psychology at McGill, a university lecturer, and a finalist for McGill 3MT and the SSHRC Storyteller competition — experiences that shaped both his research and his approach to performance under pressure.


Now, he works with technical founders, researchers, and high-performing professionals who need to communicate clearly when the stakes are real — in pitches, interviews, board meetings, and the rooms that change the trajectory of a career.

Marie-Claire Asseko — Digital Strategy & AI Consultant. Session: Agility and AI Literacy — A Non-Linear Learning Path. June 04, 2026, 4:00 PM. Online (virtual). Marie-Claire Asseko is a multilingual strategist, coach, and digital transformation operator working at the interSegment of technology, leadership, and women's economic advancement.
With over a decade of experience in SaaS, go-to-market strategy, and business process optimization, she leads two ventures: The Kaizen Gal, a coaching practice helping ambitious women navigate career transitions and step into leadership, and Meneva Digital, an agency guiding organizations through transformative technology projects.
Born in Central Africa and based in Montreal, Marie-Claire brings a rare combination of technical depth and cultural fluency to the future-of-work conversation in the AI economy; particularly for women and underrepresented communities.
Her work is grounded in a single conviction: the future belongs to those who understand the technology shaping it, and know how to translate that knowledge into action.

Ysimer (Ysi) Gonzalez — Founder of Vantelira. Session: The Experimentation Habit — The Skill That Future-Proofs You. June 03, 2026, 4:00 PM. Online (virtual). Ysimer González (Call me Ysi, pronounced "Easy") spent 18 years managing Fortune 500
supply chains — $50M+ in inventory, demand planning for millions of units, global logistics
across 20+ countries at ABB, Pratt & Whitney, and Bombardier.
She's now the founder of Vantelira Inc., a Forward Deployment Operations firm that embeds
inside growing businesses to map real processes, build operational infrastructure, and exit when
the system runs itself. Her philosophy: process before tools — always.
Industrial Engineer. Lean Six Sigma Green Belt. Based in Montréal.

Mahsa Rezaei — Future of Work Architect | Tech-Driven Social Impact Leader | TEDx Speaker. Session: Opening Keynote | Intelligent Nest & MamaNest. May 30, 2026, 2:15 PM. In-person at District3. Mahsa is a Future of Work Architect and Social Entrepreneur with over 15 years of experience, evolving from Tech to leader in building career resilience for women in the AI economy.
As founder of “MamaNest”, she has pioneered two flagship events “MamaTech AI Studio”, and the “Women's Career Conference” alongside other activities to build a comprehensive career-growth ecosystem for women. Starting with Moms, Mahsa founded the “Intelligent Nest” next to deliver AI-enhanced employment services to English-speaking women in Quebec's Professional, Scientific, and Technical Services sector.

Beyond her own ventures,She is deeply committed to the broader landscape of women's empowerment and Social Impact and has contributed to impactful initiatives including WEDO Canada, the Social Business Creation competition from HEC Montreal, and the N.E.W Venture Program. She combines technical expertise with heart-led strategy to prove that career resilience and caregiving are not mutually exclusive.

Farshad Rouhani — AI Strategy Advisor. Session: From AI-Assisted to AI-Native — Career Strategy. June 02, 2026, 4:00 PM. Online (virtual). Farshad Rouhani coaches founders and leaders through one of the most disorienting transitions of our professional lifetimes: the shift from AI-assisted work to AI-native organizations. As a Human-AI Venture Architect and Business Advisor, he's spent years helping people who weren't sure they belonged in the AI conversation realize they very much do. He advises C-suite teams on AI strategy and is known for cutting through the hype to focus on what actually builds career durability, for technologists and non-technologists alike.

Lianna Della Vecchia — Education & Program Design Specialist. Session: Welcome & Opening. May 30, 2026, 2:00 PM. In-person at District3. Lianna Della Vecchia is an education and program design specialist focused on technology, AI, and social impact. She holds a Bachelor’s degree in Communications and a Master’s in International Education, and brings over 7 years of experience working across diverse learning contexts with youth and adults.
Her work centers on designing and facilitating experiential learning programs and leading workshops on digital literacy and AI. She focuses on making complex ideas accessible and relevant through engaging, real-world learning experiences, and is particularly interested in the intersection of technology, culture and community.

Stefania Pecore — Executive Director of Women Techmakers Montreal. Session: Closing Keynote. May 30, 2026, 4:30 PM. In-person at District3. Stefania is a recognized leader in inclusive communication and responsible AI, whose career began with the introduction of the first AI and automatic translation subject at an Italian university. After earning her master's and Ph.D. in Computer Science, she applied her expertise in NLP and AI across diverse industries, from education to video games. She is a driving force behind implementing Data Governance frameworks and AI ethics principles in enterprise strategies, often guided by UNESCO recommendations. A passionate advocate for empowering women in tech, Stefania is an ambassador for Women Techmakers, Women in AI, and Women in Games, and currently serves as the Executive Director for Women Techmakers Montréal. Through her leadership, she was able to transform the event from a 150-person event to an over 400-person event, with 30 volunteers and several community partners. Her commitment to ethical AI culminated in her appointment as an AI Expert for UNESCO's Women4Ethical AI program and her subsequent election as an Ethical AI Expert Without Borders, where she helps implement UNESCO's Recommendation on the Ethics of AI worldwide. Today, she supports several founders through Don't Tech Stress with a precise mission in mind: to alleviate the tech burden, allowing founders to push their creativity to the next level. She became co-organiser of AI Tinkerers Montreal in late 2025, to support even more the builders “no fluff no deck only AI” in Montreal.
